proposals.before: Early in Zhonghe, Yang Fuguang of Zhongwu raised troops at Cai; Jian and townsman Wang Jian marched with Lu Yanhong to relieve the capital.
proposals.after: Early in Zhonghe of Tang, Zhongwu overseer Yang Fuguang raised troops at Cai; Zongquan sent his general Lu Yanhong to him; Jian and fellow townsman Wang Jian both attached themselves to Yanhong's army and entered to relieve the capital.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits Qin Zongquan sending Lu Yanhong and compresses 忠武監軍 to 'of Zhongwu'.

proposals.before: Yanhong made himself acting commissioner and made Jian Shu prefecture military commissioner.
proposals.after: Yanhong made himself acting commissioner and made Jian prefect of Shu Commandery.
proposals.reason: 刺史 is a prefect, not a military commissioner; the English also fuses Jian with the place Shu.

proposals.before: He labeled household goods with his name until he learned to read.
proposals.after: He had the names of vessels, beds, and couches written on them and, once familiar with the labels, gradually learned to read.
proposals.reason: 各題其名 means each object's own name was labeled so Jian could learn characters, not that goods were labeled with his personal name.

proposals.before: Qianning 2 he marched with Maozhen and Xingyu on the capital, forced Wang Gong on Hezhong, and killed ministers.
proposals.after: In Qianning 2 Jian with Fengxiang's Li Maozhen and Binzhou's Wang Xingyu raised troops to the capital, forced Zhaozong to request Wang Gong as Hezhong commander, and killed great ministers in the capital.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops Zhaozong as the person coerced and shortens 迫昭宗請以王珙為河中帥 to 'forced Wang Gong on Hezhong'.

proposals.before: Month 4, year 3, imperial princes attacked Maozhen, were beaten, and the emperor reached Wei Bridge.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of year 3 Zhaozong sent Prince Yan and Prince Tong with palace troops to attack Li Maozhen; they were defeated by Maozhen, and the imperial carriage reached Wei Bridge.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic replaces the named 延王 and 通王 with the generic 'imperial princes' and drops Zhaozong as the one who sent them.

proposals.before: In the second month of the fourth year, someone came to Jian reporting that Prince Mu and eight other princes below him plotted to kill Jian; Jian imprisoned the eight princes in a separate residence, discharged the twenty thousand rear palace-guard troops accompanying the emperor, and killed Pengri column chief Li Yun.
proposals.after: In the second month of the fourth year, someone came to Jian reporting that the eight princes from Prince Mu downward plotted to kill Jian; Jian imprisoned the eight princes in a separate residence, discharged the twenty thousand rear palace-guard troops accompanying the emperor, and killed Pengri column chief Li Yun.
proposals.reason: 睦王已下八王 is eight princes counted from Prince Mu down, not Prince Mu plus eight others.

proposals.before: In the eighth month Jian surrounded the Sixteen Residences with troops; Prince Tong and eleven other princes below him were all killed at Shidi Valley, reported as a treason plot.
proposals.after: In the eighth month Jian surrounded the Sixteen Residences with troops; the eleven princes from Prince Tong downward were all killed at Shidi Valley, reported as a treason plot.
proposals.reason: 通王以下十一王 is eleven princes from Prince Tong down, not Prince Tong plus eleven others.

proposals.before: Sim Ye surrendered Tongzhou; the Founder besieged Hua and Jian surrendered.
proposals.after: The vanguard reached Tongzhou; Jian's aide Sima Ye surrendered the city; the Founder then shifted troops to press Huazhou; Jian in fear begged surrender.
proposals.reason: Sim Ye is a broken rendering of 司馬鄴 (Sima Ye), and the idiomatic drops that he was Jian's 判官.

proposals.before: Old army brothers, they reconciled and Jian became Xu commissioner.
proposals.after: The Founder and Jian had long had an army-brotherhood pact; when he saw him his anger suddenly ceased, and he soon memorialized Jian as Xu military commissioner.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops the Founder, the prior anger, and that the Xu post was granted by memorial.

proposals.before: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutes》 records limited court appearances as special favor.)
proposals.after: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》: In the tenth month of Kaiping 3 an edict said Grand Preceptor Han Jian should enter the hall to offer congratulations on the first and fifteenth of each month and then attend court, and at other times not enter to be seen.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic replaces the quoted edict with a one-line summary and omits the date, office, and schedule.

proposals.before: (The 《Institutes》 praises his rule at Xuchang and forbids replacement.)
proposals.after: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》: In the first month of Qianhua 1 an edict praised Grand Preceptor Han Jian's government at Xuchang, where the people plowed and bandits stopped, and forbade the Secretariat to discuss replacing him.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic collapses a dated imperial edict into a paraphrase and drops Han Jian's name and titles.

proposals.before: Guangqi opened with Shuang campaigning against Zongquan and posting Hanzhi at Song.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Guangqi, Xizong made Shuang southeast campaign commander to strike Zongquan; Shuang then memorialized Hanzhi as deputy and posted him at Song.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits Xizong as the one who appointed Shuang and Hanzhi's deputy title.

proposals.before: After Shuang died Liu Jing held Luoyang and feared Hanzhi.
proposals.after: The next winter Zhuge Shuang died; his general Liu Jing pushed Shuang's son Zhongfang as commander; Jing feared Hanzhi hard to control and himself led troops to garrison Luoyang.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops Zhongfang, Jing's kingmaking, and that Jing feared Hanzhi.

proposals.before: He killed officer Guo Qiu and lost the army's trust.
proposals.after: Hanzhi's officers Li Tang and Guo Qiu were at odds and sought to harm each other; Hanzhi in anger executed Qiu, and army feeling was thereafter unharmonious.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits Li Tang and the mutual plot that provoked the execution.

proposals.before: and Yan Henan prefect and eastern capital regent.
proposals.after: and further memorialized Yan as Henan prefect and eastern capital acting commissioner.
proposals.reason: 'Yan Henan' fuses the person with the place; the Chinese is 又表言為河南尹.

proposals.before: Qianning 2 Keyong campaigned against Bin and Feng and made Hanzhi his deputy.
proposals.after: In Qianning 2 Li Keyong marched to resist Bin and Feng, camped north of the Wei; the Son of Heaven made Keyong Binzhou mobile-camp commander-in-chief, and Keyong then memorialized Hanzhi as deputy.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits the emperor's appointment of Keyong.

proposals.before: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Quanzhong made Hanzhi Zhaoyi commissioner.)
proposals.after: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Quanzhong memorialized Hanzhi as Zhaoyi military commissioner.)
proposals.reason: 'Hanzhi Zhaoyi' fuses the person with the army name.

proposals.before: Next year, month 6, the Founder replaced him with Ding Hui and made Hanzhi Heyang commissioner;
proposals.after: The next year, in the sixth month, as the illness grew critical, the Founder ordered Ding Hui to replace him and transferred Hanzhi as Heyang military commissioner;
proposals.reason: 'Hanzhi Heyang' fuses the person with the place, and the idiomatic drops 病篤.

proposals.before: Tianyou 1 he added Yangzhou commissioner.
proposals.after: In Tianyou 1 he concurrently led Yang Prefecture (Yangzhou 洋州) as military commissioner.
proposals.reason: 洋州 is Yang Prefecture in Shaanxi, not Yangzhou 揚州.

proposals.before: During Zhonghe, bandit Sun Xi threatened Wudang and prefect Lü Yu was helpless.
proposals.after: During Zhonghe, with Xizong in Shu, bandit chief Sun Xi gathered several thousand men wanting to enter Wudang; prefect Lü Yu was terrified and had no plan.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits Xizong in Shu and the size of Sun Xi's band.

proposals.before: Cui Yin welcomed the emperor to Danfeng Tower, led the officials in self-reproach, and wept as he memorialized, "I held high office yet failed to punish treachery; thanks to Prince of the East Zhu Quanzhong's loyal stand and killing of palace agents, Dezhao and the rest could capture the rebels and clear the palace again."
proposals.after: Cui Yin welcomed the emperor to Danfeng Tower; thanks to the Prince of Dongping, Quanzhong, Dezhao and the rest could capture the rebels.
proposals.reason: 東平王 is Prince of Dongping, not Prince of the East.

proposals.before: Early Kaiping he was posthumously named Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: Early in Kaiping he was posthumously named Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 太保 is Grand Guardian, not Grand Tutor.

proposals.before: Chenghui became Jihui and Congshi Yanbi under Maozhen's adoption.
proposals.after: Chenghui changed his name to Jihui and Congshi to Yanbi; both were adopted by Li Maozhen.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic fuses Congshi with the new name Yanbi.

proposals.before: Keyong rightly compared Hanzhi to Lü Bu.
proposals.after: Hanzhi carried a valiant air and harbored schemes of turning sides; the Martial Emperor compared him to Lü Bu—this was knowing men.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops 武皇 as speaker and the characterization 負驍雄之氣，蓄向背之謀.

decisions.after: At the beginning of the Tang dynasty's Zhonghe era, Yang Fuguang, military supervisor of the Zhongwu Army, raised troops at Cai. Qin Zongquan sent his general Lu Yanhong to join him; Han Jian and his fellow townsman Wang Jian then joined Yanhong's army and entered the capital to reinforce it.
decisions.reason: The proposed correction is substantively warranted by the Chinese, but the replacement needed clearer, more complete English and consistent title terminology.
